# Cardstock test fixture manifest

All fixtures are generated by `tools/make_fixtures.py` (re-runnable,
deterministic — 07 uses a fixed RNG seed). Every fixture's `word/styles.xml`
is canonically identical (C14N-verified) to the styles part extracted from
Verbatim 6.0.0's `Debate.dotm` (documented in `spec/verbatim-styles.md`), so Word and
Verbatim recognize all debate styles natively. Styles are applied by styleId
(`w:pStyle`/`w:rStyle`), matching what Word itself writes.

Style shorthand used below (styleId — alias): `Heading1` — Pocket,
`Heading2` — Hat, `Heading3` — Block, `Heading4` — Tag, `Style13ptBold` —
Cite (character), `StyleUnderline` — Underline (character), `Emphasis`
(character, bold+underline, not italic), `Normal` — Normal/Card.

## 01-minimal.docx (~28 KB)

Smallest complete document. One of each structural level in order:
Pocket → Hat → Block → Tag, then a single card:

- Cite paragraph (Normal): first run with `Style13ptBold` (Cite) character
  style ("Smith '24"), second run plain Normal 11 pt (full citation detail).
- Body paragraph (Normal) with: plain run, `StyleUnderline` runs, and a
  minimized run using direct formatting `w:sz w:val="16"` (8 pt, no
  underline) — the Verbatim shrink convention.

Tests: basic level detection, cite-run splitting, underline character style,
8 pt minimized text.

## 02-highlights.docx (~28 KB)

One Tag + cite + a single body paragraph containing highlighted runs inside
underlines, covering all four common highlighter colors as direct
`w:highlight` run formatting: `yellow`, `cyan` (Word "Turquoise"), `green`
(Word "Bright Green"), `magenta` (Word "Pink"). Highlighted runs also carry
the `StyleUnderline` character style; interleaved with plain-underline and
plain runs.

Tests: highlight parsing/round-trip and the Word-name vs OOXML-value mapping.

## 03-emphasis.docx (~28 KB)

One Tag + cite + body paragraph mixing:

- `Emphasis` character-style runs (Verbatim's redefinition: bold + single
  underline, explicitly NOT italic) nested between `StyleUnderline` runs,
- a run with direct bold formatting only (`w:b`, no style),
- a run with direct bold + direct underline (no character style).

Tests: distinguishing Emphasis-by-style from bold/underline-by-direct-
formatting; no-italic assumption for Emphasis.

## 04-structure.docx (~29 KB)

Structural stress test:

- Pocket "Case Negative" with two Hats; first Hat has two Blocks; Blocks hold
  multiple Tag+card units (5 cards total, distinct cites).
- A loose plain `Normal` paragraph sitting between cards (analytic note).
- A Tag directly under a Hat (no Block level) — level skipping downward.
- Pocket "Topicality" containing a Block with **no Hat above it** — level
  skipped.
- A trailing Hat with no content ("Orphan Hat") and a trailing loose plain
  paragraph at end of document.

Tests: outline-tree building with skipped/out-of-order levels, loose
paragraphs, empty headings, multiple siblings at each level.

## 05-unicode.docx (~29 KB)

Unicode and hyperlink coverage:

- Smart quotes (“ ” ‘ ’), em-dashes (—), ellipsis (…), accented Latin
  (é, ñ, ü, «guillemets»), CJK (你好) across Pocket/Hat/Block/Tag/body.
- Emoji in the cite line: "García-Márquez ’24 😎" as a `Style13ptBold` run
  (emoji is an astral-plane char — surrogate handling test), plus 🤝 in a
  minimized 8 pt run.
- A real `w:hyperlink` element with an external relationship
  (`TargetMode="External"`, non-ASCII URL) wrapping a run with the
  `Hyperlink` character style, inside the cite paragraph.

Tests: UTF-8/astral text round-trip, hyperlink relationship handling.

## 06-empty.docx (~28 KB)

No body content at all (single empty default paragraph only). The complete
Verbatim style set is still embedded.

Tests: empty-document handling; style-table reading in isolation.

## 07-large.docx (~288 KB)

Performance fixture, deterministically pseudo-random (seed `0xCA2D`):
10 Pockets × 2 Hats × 2 Blocks × 5 cards = **200 cards**. Every card has a
Tag, a two-run cite (Cite style + detail), and a body paragraph of 48
alternating segments: minimized 8 pt runs, `StyleUnderline` runs, and
yellow-highlighted underlined runs.

Tests: parser throughput/memory on a multi-hundred-KB file with ~1,400
paragraphs and ~10,000 runs.
